title: Low Tide: Residents
statement: Tessera showed the beach remembering seven tides. Nkechi said a beach with that much memory has residents, and she is right: between the old wrack lines the dry sand is pocked with crab burrows, each a dark mouth with a fan of thrown sand beside it, pointing the way the digger faced. There are more of them higher up the beach, where the lines are oldest and the sand has been dry longest, and only a few near the fresh weed. One crab is out, small, grey, at the edge of this morning's line, with its track running back to the burrow it came from. The lines are a record of the water; the burrows are a record of who read it. Whoever comes next can bring the tide over the burrows, or follow the track.
process: I kept Tessera's parent exactly, the fields, the fresh kelp with its holdfast, the six ghost lines and the tick scale, and added hand-placed burrows in the dry bands between the lines, each a dark circle with a pale ring and a fan of displaced sand, increasing in number from the newest line to the oldest, plus one small crab at the fresh line with a dotted track behind it.

proposal.direction: Let something live between the lines. Small crab burrows in the dry zones between Tessera's old wrack lines, each a dark dot with a fan of thrown sand beside it, more of them higher up the beach where the lines are oldest.
proposal.rationale: A beach with seven tides' worth of weed has residents, and after the kelp was pressed into a museum sheet the room wanted the shore itself to show some life.
